module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 5

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture5

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nontrivial V]


open scoped Classical in
/--
WOWII [Conjecture 5](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `Ls(G)` is bounded below by the maximal size
of a sphere of radius `radius(G)` around the centres of `G`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture5 (G : SimpleGraph V) (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    letI centers := { v : V | G.eccent v = G.radius }
    letI r_nat := G.radius.toNat
    letI sphere_verts (v : V) : Set V := { w | G.dist v w = r_nat }
    letI sphere_size (v : V) : ℝ := ↑(Finset.univ.filter (fun w => w ∈ sphere_verts v)).card
    letI max_sphere_size := sSup (sphere_size '' centers)
    max_sphere_size ≤ Ls G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture5

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 5 and its resolution: http://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html

WOWII glossary and references, especially definitions 1 (Ls), 9 (sphere), 13 (radius), 21 (eccentricity), 64 (centre), and reference 5: http://web.archive.org/web/20260723211215/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js

E. DeLaVina, original November 1996 list, pp. 1–2, conventions and Conjecture 5 with Fajtlowicz's stronger bound: http://web.archive.org/web/20230703190700id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII.pdf

review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration, WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture5.conjecture5. The source marks Conjecture 5 true and credits DeLaVina and Fajtlowicz (1996), consistent with `research solved`. Finite connected graphs have finite radius, centres, and spanning trees; both real suprema therefore represent attained finite maxima, and `radius.toNat` does not encounter its infinity default. Independent checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and validation.lean compile without errors, including the distance-conversion equivalence, attainment of both extrema, Ls(K₂) = 2, and maximum central sphere size 1 for K₂. Computable profiles were also tested on small complete graphs, paths, cycles, and a star. Boundary caveat: the source's terse wording omits the singleton exception. Lean's `[Nontrivial V]` excludes K₁, where the source's degree-one leaf convention gives Ls = 0 but the radius-zero sphere has size 1. I regard this as making the necessary intended domain restriction explicit, rather than a substantive defect. No repository files were modified.
